```python
    .add_source(EntsoeSource(country_code="PL", api_key=ENTSOE_API_KEY, type=["load", "price"]))
    # jma_seamless (default model) is only leak-free up to 5 days ahead at the default run="00"; see "Horizon
    # limit" under OpenMeteoSource above.
    .add_source(OpenMeteoSource(latitude=52.2297, longitude=21.0122, horizon=5, prefix="warsaw"))
    .add_source(CalendarSource(country="PL", holidays="binary", weekday="onehot", daylight=True))
    .add_transformer(ResampleTransformer(freq="1h"))
    .add_transformer(LagTransformer(columns=["load_actual"], lags=[1, 2, 7], freq="day"))
    .add_validator(CoverageValidator(columns=["load_actual", "price"], min_coverage=1.0))
)

df = pipeline.run(start="2023-01-01", end="2024-04-01", cache=True)
df.to_csv("data.csv")
```

## Example 2: Model Pipeline Only

```python
import os
os.environ["THREADS_PER_PROCESS"] = "16"
os.environ["MAX_PROCESSES"] = "4"
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"

import pandas as pd
from epftoolbox2.pipelines import ModelPipeline
from epftoolbox2.models import OLSModel, LassoCVModel
from epftoolbox2.evaluators import MAEEvaluator, RMSEEvaluator, rMAEEvaluator
from epftoolbox2.exporters import ExcelExporter, TerminalExporter, CsvExporter

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv", index_col=0)
df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index, utc=True).tz_convert("Europe/Warsaw")  # back to the local zone

seasonal_indicators = [
    "is_monday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_tuesday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_wednesday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_thursday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_friday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_saturday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_sunday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_holiday_d+{horizon}",
    "daylight_hours_d+{horizon}",
]

predictors = [
    *seasonal_indicators,
    "load_actual_d-1",
    "load_actual_d-7",
    "warsaw_temperature_2m_d+{horizon}",
]

pipeline = (
    ModelPipeline()
    .add_model(OLSModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, name="OLS Baseline"))
    .add_model(LassoCVModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, cv=5, name="Lasso CV"))
    .add_evaluator(MAEEvaluator())
    .add_evaluator(RMSEEvaluator())
    .add_evaluator(rMAEEvaluator(base_model="OLS Baseline"))
    .add_exporter(TerminalExporter())
    .add_exporter(ExcelExporter("results.xlsx"))
    .add_exporter(CsvExporter("results.csv", extra_columns=["is_holiday"]))
)

report = pipeline.run(
    data=df,
    test_start="2024-02-01",
    test_end="2024-03-01",
    target="price",
    horizon=5,  # matches warsaw_temperature_2m's leak-free horizon (see the OpenMeteoSource in Example 1)
    save_dir="results",
)

print(report.summary())
print(report.by_horizon())
```

## Example 3: Full Workflow (Code)

```python
import os
os.environ["PYTHON_GIL"] = "0"
os.environ["THREADS_PER_PROCESS"] = "16"
os.environ["MAX_PROCESSES"] = "4"
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"

from epftoolbox2.pipelines import DataPipeline, ModelPipeline
from epftoolbox2.data.sources import EntsoeSource, OpenMeteoSource, CalendarSource
from epftoolbox2.data.transformers import ResampleTransformer, LagTransformer
from epftoolbox2.data.validators import CoverageValidator
from epftoolbox2.models import OLSModel, LassoCVModel
from epftoolbox2.evaluators import MAEEvaluator
from epftoolbox2.exporters import ExcelExporter, TerminalExporter

ENTSOE_API_KEY = os.environ.get("ENTSOE_API_KEY")

data_pipeline = (
    DataPipeline(timezone="Europe/Warsaw")
    .add_source(EntsoeSource(country_code="PL", api_key=ENTSOE_API_KEY, type=["load", "price"]))
    # jma_seamless (default model) is only leak-free up to 5 days ahead at the default run="00"; see "Horizon
    # limit" under OpenMeteoSource above.
    .add_source(OpenMeteoSource(latitude=52.2297, longitude=21.0122, horizon=5, prefix="warsaw"))
    .add_source(CalendarSource(country="PL", holidays="binary", weekday="onehot", daylight=True))
    .add_transformer(ResampleTransformer(freq="1h"))
    .add_transformer(LagTransformer(columns=["load_actual", "price"], lags=[1, 2, 7], freq="day"))
    # Calendar features are known arbitrarily far in advance, so d+0..d+7 is safe.
    .add_transformer(
        LagTransformer(
            lags=range(-7, 1),
            freq="day",
            columns=[
                "is_monday", "is_tuesday", "is_wednesday", "is_thursday",
                "is_friday", "is_saturday", "is_sunday", "is_holiday", "daylight_hours",
            ],
        )
    )
    .add_validator(CoverageValidator(columns=["load_actual", "price"], min_coverage=1.0))
)

df = data_pipeline.run(start="2023-05-01", end="2024-07-01", cache=True)

seasonal_indicators = [
    "is_monday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_tuesday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_wednesday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_thursday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_friday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_saturday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_sunday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_holiday_d+{horizon}",
    "daylight_hours_d+{horizon}",
]

predictors = [
    *seasonal_indicators,
    "load_actual_d-1",
    "load_actual_d-2",
    "price_d-1",
    "price_d-2",
    lambda h: f"warsaw_temperature_2m_d+{h}",
]

model_pipeline = (
    ModelPipeline()
    .add_model(OLSModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, name="OLS"))
    .add_model(LassoCVModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, cv=5, name="LassoCV"))
    .add_evaluator(MAEEvaluator())
    .add_exporter(TerminalExporter())
    .add_exporter(ExcelExporter("results.xlsx"))
)

report = model_pipeline.run(
    data=df,
    test_start="2024-06-01",
    test_end="2024-06-30",
    target="price",
    horizon=5,  # matches warsaw_temperature_2m's leak-free horizon (see the OpenMeteoSource above)
    save_dir="results",
)

print(report.summary())
print(report.by_horizon())
```

## Example 4: Workflow (YAML-based)

```python
import os
os.environ["PYTHON_GIL"] = "0"

from epftoolbox2.pipelines import DataPipeline, ModelPipeline, Workflow
from epftoolbox2.data.sources import EntsoeSource, OpenMeteoSource, CalendarSource
from epftoolbox2.data.transformers import ResampleTransformer, LagTransformer
from epftoolbox2.data.validators import CoverageValidator
from epftoolbox2.models import OLSModel, LassoCVModel
from epftoolbox2.evaluators import MAEEvaluator
from epftoolbox2.exporters import ExcelExporter, TerminalExporter

ENTSOE_API_KEY = os.environ.get("ENTSOE_API_KEY")

# Phase 1: build and save config (run once)
predictors = [
    "is_monday_d+{horizon}", "is_tuesday_d+{horizon}", "is_wednesday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_thursday_d+{horizon}", "is_friday_d+{horizon}", "is_saturday_d+{horizon}",
    "is_sunday_d+{horizon}", "is_holiday_d+{horizon}", "daylight_hours_d+{horizon}",
    "load_actual_d-1", "load_actual_d-2", "price_d-1", "price_d-2",
    "warsaw_temperature_2m_d+{horizon}",
]

(
    DataPipeline(timezone="Europe/Warsaw")
    .add_source(EntsoeSource(country_code="PL", api_key=ENTSOE_API_KEY, type=["load", "price"]))
    # jma_seamless (default model) is only leak-free up to 5 days ahead at the default run="00"; see "Horizon
    # limit" under OpenMeteoSource above.
    .add_source(OpenMeteoSource(latitude=52.2297, longitude=21.0122, horizon=5, prefix="warsaw"))
    .add_source(CalendarSource(country="PL", holidays="binary", daylight=True, weekday="onehot"))
    .add_transformer(ResampleTransformer(freq="1h"))
    .add_transformer(LagTransformer(columns=["load_actual", "price"], lags=[1, 2, 7], freq="day"))
    # Calendar features are known arbitrarily far in advance, so d+0..d+7 is safe.
    .add_transformer(
        LagTransformer(
            lags=range(-7, 1),
            freq="day",
            columns=[
                "is_monday", "is_tuesday", "is_wednesday", "is_thursday",
                "is_friday", "is_saturday", "is_sunday", "is_holiday", "daylight_hours",
            ],
        )
    )
    # load_forecast (A65/A01) is published 10:00 CET the day before delivery: only d+1 is ever safe.
    .add_transformer(LagTransformer(lags=range(-1, 0), freq="day", columns=["load_forecast"]))
    .add_validator(CoverageValidator(columns=["load_actual", "price"], min_coverage=1.0))
    .save("data_pipeline.yaml")
)

(
    ModelPipeline()
    .add_model(OLSModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, name="OLS"))
    .add_model(LassoCVModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, cv=5, name="LassoCV"))
    .add_evaluator(MAEEvaluator())
    .add_exporter(TerminalExporter())
    .add_exporter(ExcelExporter("workflow_results.xlsx"))
    .save("model_pipeline.yaml")
)

Workflow(
    data_pipeline="data_pipeline.yaml",
    model_pipeline="model_pipeline.yaml",
    data_start="2023-05-01",
    data_end="2024-08-01",
    data_cache=True,
    model_test_start="2024-06-01",
    model_test_end="2024-07-01",
    model_target="price",
    model_horizon=5,  # matches warsaw_temperature_2m's leak-free horizon (see the OpenMeteoSource above)
    max_processes=4,
    threads_per_process=8,
).save("experiment.yaml")

# Phase 2: load and run (cluster job, only this line needed)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    report = Workflow.load("experiment.yaml").run()
    print(report.summary())
    print(report.by_horizon())
```

---

## Example 5: Forecast-Only (Operational Daily Forecast)

```python
import os
os.environ["THREADS_PER_PROCESS"] = "8"
os.environ["MAX_PROCESSES"] = "2"

from epftoolbox2.pipelines import DataPipeline, ModelPipeline
from epftoolbox2.data.sources import EntsoeSource, OpenMeteoSource, CalendarSource
from epftoolbox2.data.transformers import TimezoneTransformer, ResampleTransformer, LagTransformer
from epftoolbox2.models import OLSModel, LassoCVModel

ENTSOE_API_KEY = os.environ.get("ENTSOE_API_KEY")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Date keywords resolve at runtime, so this script can run every day without changing anything.
    # "now_d-730" is 2 years ago, "today_d+5" is 5 days from now.
    # Adjust the -N offset to cover your largest model's training_window.
    # "end" always covers the whole day it names, so "today_d+5" includes all 24 hours of the
    # last horizon day. timezone="Europe/Warsaw" makes that day the market's own local day.
    df = (
        DataPipeline(timezone="Europe/Warsaw")
        .add_source(EntsoeSource(country_code="PL", api_key=ENTSOE_API_KEY, type=["load", "price"]))
        # jma_seamless (default model) is only leak-free up to 5 days ahead at the default run="00"; see
        # "Horizon limit" under OpenMeteoSource above.
        .add_source(OpenMeteoSource(latitude=52.2297, longitude=21.0122, horizon=5, prefix="warsaw"))
        .add_source(CalendarSource(country="PL", holidays="binary", weekday="onehot", daylight=True))
        .add_transformer(TimezoneTransformer())
        .add_transformer(ResampleTransformer(freq="1h"))
        .add_transformer(LagTransformer(columns=["load_actual", "price"], lags=[1, 2, 7], freq="day"))
        # Calendar features are known arbitrarily far in advance, so d+0..d+7 is safe.
        .add_transformer(LagTransformer(
            lags=range(-7, 1), freq="day",
            columns=["is_monday", "is_tuesday", "is_wednesday", "is_thursday",
                     "is_friday", "is_saturday", "is_sunday", "is_holiday",
                     "daylight_hours"],
        ))
        # load_forecast (A65/A01) is published 10:00 CET the day before delivery: only d+1 is ever safe.
        .add_transformer(LagTransformer(lags=range(-1, 0), freq="day", columns=["load_forecast"]))
        .run(start="now_d-730", end="today_d+5", cache=True)
    )

    predictors = [
        "is_monday_d+{horizon}", "is_tuesday_d+{horizon}", "is_wednesday_d+{horizon}",
        "is_thursday_d+{horizon}", "is_friday_d+{horizon}", "is_saturday_d+{horizon}",
        "is_sunday_d+{horizon}", "is_holiday_d+{horizon}", "daylight_hours_d+{horizon}",
        "load_actual_d-1", "load_actual_d-2", "price_d-1", "price_d-2",
        "warsaw_temperature_2m_d+{horizon}",
    ]

    report = (
        ModelPipeline()
        .add_model(OLSModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, name="OLS"))
        .add_model(LassoCVModel(predictors=predictors, training_window=365, cv=7, name="LassoCV"))
        .run(
            data=df,
            test_start="today",   # resolve_date("today") → today's ISO date at runtime
            test_end="today",
            target="price",
            horizon=5,  # matches warsaw_temperature_2m's leak-free horizon (see the OpenMeteoSource above)
            forecast_only=True,   # skips evaluators and exporters
        )
    )

    # 120 rows per model (24h × 5 horizons), sorted by model → horizon → hour
    forecast = report.predictions()
    print(forecast)
```

---

# API REFERENCE

## DataPipeline

```python
class DataPipeline:
    def __init__(
        self,
        sources: Optional[List[DataSource]] = None,
        transformers: Optional[List[Transformer]] = None,
        validators: Optional[List[Validator]] = None,        # run on the final (post-transformer) frame
        source_validators: Optional[List[Validator]] = None,  # run on raw source output, before any transformer
        timezone: Optional[str] = None,   # e.g. "Europe/Warsaw"; makes run() dates mean local calendar days.
                                           # The single place the market zone needs to be written: components
                                           # whose own zone decides a local day (TimezoneTransformer.target_tz,
                                           # Calendar/OpenMeteo*.timezone) inherit it when left unset; an
                                           # explicit, different zone still raises.
        on_invalid: str = "warn",         # "warn" (log and continue) or "raise" (raise DataValidationError)
    ): ...

    def add_source(self, source: DataSource) -> "DataPipeline": ...
    def add_transformer(self, transformer: Transformer) -> "DataPipeline": ...
    def add_validator(self, validator: Validator) -> "DataPipeline": ...
    def add_source_validator(self, validator: Validator) -> "DataPipeline": ...

    validation_results: Dict[str, ValidationResult]  # keyed "source_validators.<Class>"/"validators.<Class>", reset each run()

    def run(
        self,
        start: Union[str, pd.Timestamp],  # "YYYY-MM-DD", Timestamp, or "today", "now_d-730" (see Timezone below)
        end: Union[str, pd.Timestamp],    # Same. Use "today_d+7" to include weather forecast window (see Timezone)
        cache: Union[bool, str] = False,  # True (per-source cache), False, or a file/directory path
    ) -> pd.DataFrame: ...

    def save(self, path: Union[str, Path], include_secrets: bool = False) -> None: ...   # Save to YAML

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Union[str, Path]) -> "DataPipeline": ...  # Load from YAML
```

### Timezone and Date Semantics

- A date-only `start`/`end` (a string, or "today"/"now_d±N") always names a **whole calendar day**: `start`
  begins at that day's midnight and `end` runs through the end of its own day (inclusive). `end="today_d+7"`
  therefore includes all 24 hours of the 7th day ahead, the natural choice for a `horizon=7` forecast-only run.
- `timezone=None` (default): those days are **UTC** days.
- `timezone="Europe/Warsaw"` (or any IANA zone): those days are **local calendar days** instead, correctly sized
  on DST-transition days (23/25 hours). Naive timestamps passed to `run()` are read as local instants, and
  timezone-aware timestamps are used as given.
- `timezone` is also the single place the market zone needs to be written: `TimezoneTransformer.target_tz`,
  `CalendarSource`/`OpenMeteoSource`'s own zone may all be
  left unset (`None`) and they then inherit it, checked and bound at construction and again at the start of
  `run()` (so `add_transformer`/`add_source` can't introduce a mismatch unnoticed). An explicitly set, different
  zone still raises `ValueError`: `timezone` decides what a local calendar day is, and a component computing its
  own local time in a different zone would silently disagree with it. A component that needs a zone and has
  neither raises a clear error when the pipeline runs. `CsvSource.timezone` is excluded (it is the input file's
  own zone, not the market's).
- Two sources producing the same column name raise `ValueError` naming both sources (e.g. give one a `prefix`).

## ModelPipeline

```python
class ModelPipeline:
    def __init__(
        self,
        information_set: Optional[InformationSet] = None,   # Overrides issue_time/issue_timezone below
        issue_time: Optional[str] = None,                    # Shortcut: builds InformationSet(issue_time, issue_timezone)
        issue_timezone: str = "Europe/Brussels",              # Zone of issue_time, ignored if information_set is given
    ): ...

    def add_model(self, model: BaseModel) -> "ModelPipeline": ...
    def add_evaluator(self, evaluator: Evaluator) -> "ModelPipeline": ...
    def add_exporter(self, exporter: Exporter) -> "ModelPipeline": ...

    def run(
        self,
        data: pd.DataFrame,              # DataFrame with DatetimeIndex
        test_start: Optional[str] = None,  # Test period start ("YYYY-MM-DD" or "today", "now_d-7"); required unless forecast_only=True
        test_end: Optional[str] = None,    # Test period end; required unless forecast_only=True
        target: str = "price",            # Target column name
        horizon: int = 7,                 # Max forecast horizon (days)
        freq: str = "1h",                 # "1h" or "15min"; must match the data
        save_dir: Optional[str] = None,   # Directory for incremental results
        forecast_only: bool = False,      # Skip evaluators and exporters; use report.predictions()
        allow_manifest_mismatch: bool = False,  # Overwrite and resume despite a manifest disagreement
        require_manifest: bool = False,   # Refuse (not warn) to resume results with no manifest
    ) -> EvaluationReport: ...

    def report(                           # Report from the JSONL files in save_dir, runs evaluators/exporters
        self,
        save_dir: Union[str, Path],
        test_start: Optional[str] = None,
        test_end: Optional[str] = None,
        horizon: int = 7,
        freq: str = "1h",
        forecast_only: bool = False,
        data: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,   # only for exporters that join source columns
        allow_missing: bool = False,           # else FileNotFoundError when a model has no results
    ) -> EvaluationReport: ...

    def save(self, path: Union[str, Path]) -> None: ...   # Save to YAML

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Union[str, Path]) -> "ModelPipeline": ...  # Load from YAML
```

## Workflow

```python
class Workflow:
    def __init__(
        self,
        data_start: str,
        data_end: str,
        model_test_start: Optional[str] = None,   # Required unless model_forecast_only=True
        model_test_end: Optional[str] = None,     # Required unless model_forecast_only=True
        data_pipeline: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,   # Path to data_pipeline.yaml
        model_pipeline: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,  # Path to model_pipeline.yaml
        data_cache: Union[bool, str] = False,
        model_target: str = "price",
        model_horizon: int = 7,
        model_freq: str = "1h",                             # "1h" or "15min"; must match the data's resolution
        model_forecast_only: bool = False,                  # Skip evaluators/exporters; use report.predictions()
        max_processes: Optional[int] = None,
        threads_per_process: Optional[int] = None,
        cache_path: Optional[str] = None,                   # Overrides data_cache if set
        model_index: Optional[int] = None,                  # Run only models[model_index]; all models if None
        model_save_dir: Optional[str] = None,               # YAML model_pipeline.save_dir; required with model_index
        model_allow_manifest_mismatch: bool = False,        # Resume into model_save_dir despite a manifest mismatch
        model_require_manifest: bool = False,               # Refuse (not warn) to resume results with no manifest
    ): ...

    def run(self) -> EvaluationReport: ...
    def report(self, allow_missing: bool = False) -> EvaluationReport: ...  # merge save_dir after an array job

    def save(self, path: Union[str, Path]) -> None: ...

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Union[str, Path]) -> "Workflow": ...
```

---

## EvaluationReport

```python
class EvaluationReport:
    def summary(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...          # model, forecasts, metrics
    def forecast_counts(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...  # model, planned, produced, missing, skip reasons
    def by_hour(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def by_horizon(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def by_hour_horizon(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def by_year(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def by_year_horizon(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def by_run_weekday_horizon(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...    # grouped by the issue day's weekday × horizon
    def by_target_weekday_horizon(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...  # grouped by the target day's weekday × horizon
    def predictions(self) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    # Returns tidy DataFrame sorted by model→horizon→hour.
    # Columns: run_date, target_date, hour, horizon, prediction, model
    # No "actual" column: use for forecast_only=True runs.
    def iter_details(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[str, pd.DataFrame]]: ...
    def compute_all(self) -> Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]: ...
    # {"summary": ..., "hour": ..., "horizon": ..., "hour_horizon": ..., "year": ..., "year_horizon": ...,
    #  "run_weekday_horizon": ..., "target_weekday_horizon": ...} in one pass; used by ExcelExporter.
```

---

# ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES

Must be set **before** any library imports (especially before numpy/sklearn are imported).

```python
import os
os.environ["PYTHON_GIL"] = "0"            # Enable free-threading (Python 3.13t+, or -Xgil=0)
os.environ["MAX_PROCESSES"] = "4"         # Worker processes (default: cpu_count // THREADS_PER_PROCESS)
os.environ["THREADS_PER_PROCESS"] = "16"  # Threads per worker process (alias: MAX_THREADS)
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"       # Prevent BLAS oversubscription (always recommended)
```

`Workflow.run()` always sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`, `BLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`, and `PYTHON_GIL=0` automatically, and applies `MAX_PROCESSES`/`THREADS_PER_PROCESS` from its config. `model_index` is expanded from env vars at `load()` time (e.g. `$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`) and selects a single model by index, all models run if omitted. For code-only usage (no Workflow), set thread vars manually before imports.

# SUPPORTED COUNTRIES

## ENTSOE Countries
AL, AT, BA, BE, BG, BY, CH, CZ, DE, DE_50HZ, DE_AMPRION, DE_AT_LU, DE_LU, DE_TENNET, DE_TRANSNET, DK, DK_1, DK_2, EE, ES, FI, FR, GB, GB_ELECLINK, GB_IFA, GB_IFA2, GB_NIR, GE, GR, HR, HU, IE, IE_SEM, IS, IT, IT_* (many regions), LT, LU, LV, MD, ME, MK, MT, NL, NO, NO_1-5, PL, PT, RO, RS, RU, SE, SE_1-4, SI, SK, TR, UA, UK, XK

## CalendarSource Countries (Holidays)
AT, BE, BG, CH, CZ, DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, GB, GR, HU, IE, IT, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SE, SK

---

# COMMON PITFALLS

## NaN Values in Predictors
Models will fail with `ValueError: Input X contains NaN` if predictors have null values. Solutions:
1. Ensure sufficient lag data exists (check training window)
2. Choose predictors that exist for all rows
3. Use `CoverageValidator` to catch issues early

## Callable Predictors and YAML
Callable predictors cannot be serialized to YAML. Use `"{horizon}"` string templates instead:
```python
# Instead of: lambda h: f"warsaw_temperature_2m_d+{h}"
# Use:        "warsaw_temperature_2m_d+{horizon}"
```

## Timezone Handling
- Sources return UTC
- Use TimezoneTransformer for local time. Order: TimezoneTransformer → ResampleTransformer → LagTransformer
- DST days keep 23 or 25 local hours. ResampleTransformer does not create the missing 02:00 row
- ResampleTransformer fills only slots it creates by upsampling. Real gaps stay NaN

## Column Naming
- Lag columns: `{column}_{unit}-{lag}` (e.g., `load_actual_d-1`)
- Forward lags (negative): `{column}_{unit}+{abs(lag)}` (e.g., `load_actual_d+7`)
- Weather forecasts: `{prefix}_{variable}_d+{horizon}` (e.g., `warsaw_temperature_2m_d+1`)
- Predictor templates use `{horizon}` placeholder, replaced with 1, 2, ..., horizon

## Date Keywords
`DataPipeline.run()`, `ModelPipeline.run()`, `BaseModel.run()`, and `Workflow` all accept date keywords:
- `"today"` / `"now"` → today's date
- `"today_d+7"` / `"now_d+7"` → today + 7 days
- `"now_d-730"` → today − 730 days
- The offset `N` in `_d±N` is any integer. Use any value to match your training window.
- Normal ISO date strings (`"2024-01-01"`) pass through unchanged.
- `ModelPipeline.run()`, `BaseModel.run()` and `Workflow` resolve "today" as the machine's local date
  (`datetime.date.today()`, implemented in `epftoolbox2/_date_utils.py:resolve_date()`).
  `DataPipeline.run()` resolves it the same way when `timezone` is not set (and `end` then covers the whole
  UTC day it names). With `timezone="Europe/Warsaw"` (etc.) set, it uses today's date **in that zone** instead,
  and `end` covers the whole local day it names. See "Timezone and Date Semantics" under DataPipeline in API
  REFERENCE.

## Windows Multiprocessing
Windows uses `spawn` context (not `fork`). Scripts must use `if __name__ == '__main__':` guard.

## Memory with Large Datasets
- Use `cache=True` to avoid re-downloading
- Use `save_dir` for incremental model training
- Set `THREADS_PER_PROCESS` and `MAX_PROCESSES` appropriately for your system

---

# EXTENDING THE LIBRARY

## Custom DataSource

```python
from epftoolbox2.data.sources.base import DataSource

class MySource(DataSource):
    def __init__(self, my_param: str):
        self.my_param = my_param  # Store constructor params as-is (no derived public attrs)
        self._validate_config()

    def _validate_config(self) -> bool:
        return True

    def fetch(self, start: pd.Timestamp, end: pd.Timestamp) -> pd.DataFrame:
        # Return DataFrame with DatetimeIndex (UTC) covering at least [start, end)
        ...

    def get_cache_config(self) -> Optional[dict]:
        # Every parameter that changes the output; bump schema_version when parsing changes
        return {"source_type": "my_source", "param": self.my_param, "schema_version": 1}
```

Register in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY["sources"]` in `data_pipeline.py` for YAML support.

## Custom Transformer

```python
from epftoolbox2.data.transformers.base import Transformer

class MyTransformer(Transformer):
    def transform(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        ...
```

Register in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY["transformers"]` in `data_pipeline.py`.

## Custom Validator

```python
from epftoolbox2.data.validators.base import Validator
from epftoolbox2.data.validators.result import ValidationResult

class MyValidator(Validator):
    def validate(self, df: pd.DataFrame) -> ValidationResult:
        result = ValidationResult()
        return result
```

Register in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY["validators"]` in `data_pipeline.py`.

## Custom Model

```python
from epftoolbox2.models.base import BaseModel

class MyModel(BaseModel):
    def _fit_predict(self, train_x, train_y, test_x) -> Tuple[float, list]:
        # Fit model, return (prediction, coefficients)
        ...
```

Register in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY["models"]` in `model_pipeline.py`.

## Custom Evaluator

```python
from epftoolbox2.evaluators.base import Evaluator

class MyEvaluator(Evaluator):
    name = "MyMetric"

    def compute(self, df: pd.DataFrame, **kwargs) -> float:
        return ...
```

The `**kwargs` may include `model_dfs` (Dict[str, DataFrame]), all model DataFrames for the current data slice, enabling cross-model metrics like rMAE.

Register in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY["evaluators"]` in `model_pipeline.py`.

## Custom Exporter

```python
from epftoolbox2.exporters.base import Exporter

class MyExporter(Exporter):
    def export(self, report: EvaluationReport) -> None:
        ...
```

Register in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY["exporters"]` in `model_pipeline.py`.

---

# CLI

Installed automatically with the package. Available as `epf` on PATH after `pip install epftoolbox2`.

## Commands

### `epf` (no arguments)
Launches an interactive wizard. Arrow-key menus + text prompts, no YAML required.

**Main menu options:**
- Run experiment / data pipeline / model pipeline from an existing YAML
- Build & run data pipeline interactively (sources → transformers → validators → dates → output CSV → save YAML → run)
- Build & run model pipeline interactively (CSV input + column detection → models → evaluators → exporters → test period → save YAML → run)

### `epf run <experiment.yaml>`
Run a full Workflow YAML.

```bash
epf run experiment.yaml
epf run experiment.yaml --model-index $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID   # SLURM array
epf run experiment.yaml --processes 4 --threads 8
epf run experiment.yaml --dry-run   # validate config only
```

Flags: `--model-index N` (needs `model_pipeline.save_dir`), `--processes N`, `--threads N`, `--dry-run`

### `epf report <experiment.yaml>`
Merge the per-model JSONL files in `model_pipeline.save_dir` (after a SLURM array) and run the evaluators and
exporters once. Prints planned vs produced forecasts per model. `--allow-missing` reports the models that have
results instead of failing.

### `epf data <data_pipeline.yaml>`
Run a DataPipeline and save result to CSV.

```bash
epf data data_pipeline.yaml --start 2022-01-01 --end 2024-01-01 --output data.csv
epf data data_pipeline.yaml --start 2022-01-01 --end 2024-01-01 --output data.csv --cache .cache/
```

Required flags: `--start DATE`, `--end DATE`, `--output FILE`
Optional flags: `--cache PATH`

The CSV names its time zone in the index header (e.g. `datetime[Europe/Warsaw]`). `epf model` and the TUI read it
back in that zone.

### `epf model <model_pipeline.yaml>`
Run a ModelPipeline on an existing CSV.

```bash
epf model model_pipeline.yaml \
    --data data.csv \
    --test-start 2023-01-01 \
    --test-end 2024-01-01 \
    --target price \
    --horizon 7 \
    --save-dir results/ \
    --forecast-only
```

Required flags: `--data FILE`, `--test-start DATE`, `--test-end DATE`
Optional flags: `--target COL` (default: price), `--horizon N` days (default: 7), `--freq {1h,15min}` (default: 1h),
`--tz ZONE` (local zone of the data, needed for CSVs with UTC offsets but no zone in the header), `--save-dir DIR`,
`--forecast-only`, `--issue-time HH:MM` and `--issue-timezone ZONE` (information set, overrides the YAML),
`--allow-manifest-mismatch` (resume even if `--save-dir`'s manifest disagrees with this run, overwriting it),
`--require-manifest` (refuse to resume from a `--save-dir` with results but no manifest, instead of warning)

### `epf validate <file.yaml>`
Auto-detect YAML type (Workflow / DataPipeline / ModelPipeline), load, and instantiate all components. Exits 1 on error.

```bash
epf validate data_pipeline.yaml
epf validate experiment.yaml
```

### `epf init`
Scaffold template `experiment.yaml`, `data_pipeline.yaml`, `model_pipeline.yaml` in the current directory.

```bash
epf init
epf init --force   # overwrite existing files
```

## Typical split workflow

```bash
# Step 1: fetch data once, cache it
epf data data_pipeline.yaml --start 2020-01-01 --end 2024-01-01 --output data.csv

# Step 2: iterate on model config
epf model model_pipeline.yaml \
    --data data.csv \
    --test-start 2023-01-01 \
    --test-end 2024-01-01
```
